sections.heading: What changed from 1.12
sections.html:
• Pets copy 10% of your attack power and all of your crit.
  • Aimed Shot: trained, 2 second cast, one 6 second cooldown shared with Multi-Shot. Auto shots keep firing while you cast it.
  • Aimed Shot over Multi-Shot every time the cooldown comes up. Multi-Shot is for packs and for when you have to move.
  • Heart of the Lion from level 1: 10% stats and 280 melee and ranged attack power at 60 for everyone near you, and another 10% stats for you.
  • Aspect of the Beast gives melee attack power. Survival runs it; Hawk stays the ranged aspect.
  • Trueshot Aura: ranged attack power only, 100 at 60, party and raid.

sections.heading: What changed from 1.12
sections.html:
• Personal debuffs. Improved Scorch and Winter’s Chill now only boost your own spells. Every Fire mage keeps their own Scorch stacks, and nobody else’s Scorches help you.
  • Ice Block comes earlier. It is still a Frost talent, but it sits at 15 points instead of 20, with Cold Snap below it now. Fire mages never get there, and the Arcane builds have no spare point for it, so only Frost mages carry Ice Block.
  • Armor and threat. Raid in Mage Armor, which now keeps half your mana regeneration running while you cast; Ice Armor is for when things hit you. There is no Molten Armor or Invisibility, so threat is handled with Arcane Subtlety, Burning Soul and Frost Channeling, and by not out-casting your tank.
  • One hit stat. Hit now counts for spells and attacks alike, and Precision in the Frost tree adds 6% hit to every school where 1.12’s Elemental Precision covered only Fire and Frost, which is why the Arcane and Fire builds both dip three points there.
  • New spells. Arcane Blast, Arcane Wrath, Ice Lance on an 8 second cooldown, Heating Up, Fingers of Frost and Missile Barrage are new talents, Frostfire Bolt is trained at 40, 50 and 60, and Teleport: Dalaran at 50.

sections.heading: Races
sections.html:
• Orc Mage is new for Forever and gives the Horde a third mage race, with Blood Fury’s spell power on a 2 minute cooldown.
  • Skyborne can be mages too, but only the Alliance High Order Skyborne; the Horde Windshapers cannot.
  • On the Alliance, Arcane and Frost take a Gnome: Eureka! makes your damage spells, all but Arcane Wrath, hit 10% harder and cost 10% less for 8 seconds, every 2 minutes. Arcane Power comes back every 3, so pair Eureka! with it whenever both are ready. Fire takes a Human: Ruthless adds 1% crit, which Fire turns into Ignite. On the Horde, Undead is the pick for all three specs, with Orc close behind.

sections.heading: Raids and leveling
sections.html: Fire builds its Scorch stacks and burns into a big Combustion and needs every gem, potion and rune on a long fight, Arcane puts the most damage into its Arcane Power windows, and Frost is the easiest to level and the safest in a bad pull.

sections.heading: What changed from 1.12
sections.html:
• Every priest now has Fear Ward, Devouring Plague, Shadow Word: Death, Divine Spirit and Lightwell from the trainer.
  • Penance and Prayer of Mending are the deep Discipline and Holy talents, and the trainer teaches their higher ranks once you have them.
  • Shadowfiend, the Season of Discovery rune, is not in Forever.
  • Low-rank heals. In Forever a rank learned far below your level gets less of your healing bonus, and the Spell Healing tooltip on your character sheet says so. At 60, Lesser Heal and the first ranks of Renew and Heal get next to nothing from your gear: downrank only within the ranks you learned in your forties and fifties.

sections.heading: Races
sections.html:
Race picks.

  • Discipline: Human on Alliance for The Human Spirit and Divine Grace, with Gnome level with it at 60. Undead on Horde for Dark Sacrifice.
  • Holy: Human on Alliance for The Human Spirit and Divine Grace, with Gnome close. Undead on Horde for Dark Sacrifice.
  • Shadow: Human on Alliance for Ruthless, with Night Elf just as good and Dwarf close. Undead on Horde for Touch of the Grave, well ahead of Troll.
  • The Gnome priest is new. Gnomes bring Eureka! (8 seconds of 10% cheaper and 10% stronger direct heals and damage spells every 2 minutes, and 10% stronger Mind Flay and Penance ticks; never Shadow Word: Pain, Devouring Plague, Renew or a shield), Expansive Mind (5% more mana) and Escape Artist. Their priest spells are Contingency Plan, a ward that shields and heals an ally who drops under 35%, and Confounding Flash, which confuses nearby enemies. At 60 a Gnome heals as well as a Human as Discipline.

Each race has its own two priest spells.

  • Human: Divine Grace (a free instant heal that clears Weakened Soul) and Feedback.
  • Dwarf: Desperate Prayer and Chastise.
  • Night Elf: Elune’s Grace and Starshards.
  • Undead: Dark Sacrifice (health for mana, once a fight) and Touch of Weakness.
  • Troll: Hex of Weakness and Shadowguard.

Skyborne cannot be priests.

overview.strengths:
• Lone Wolf’s 20% damage on every attack, with no pet to keep alive
  • Expose Prey opens Mongoose Bite off your own hits on a marked target, so it fires even on a boss that never swings at you
  • Resourcefulness takes 60% off your melee and trap costs, so you do not run dry
  • Rapid Fire speeds your melee swings
overview.weaknesses:
• You stand in melee with the rogues and warriors, so cleaves, frontal breaths and melee-range mechanics are yours to dodge
  • Two weapons and a white hit cap well above a ranged hunter’s make hit hard to fill
overview.raid:
• Role: Melee DPS, with your pet dismissed
  • Brings: Heart of the Lion (more stats and a flat attack power bonus for everyone near you) and Hunter’s Mark on the boss
  • What the raid adds: Forever’s Strength of Earth Totem gives less Strength than Era’s and Curse of Recklessness strips less armor, so a full raid lifts a Survival hunter less than it did in Era.

talents.prose:
Thirty-three points in Survival take every melee damage talent, thirteen in Marksmanship take Careful Aim, Rapid Killing and Lone Wolf, and five in Beast Mastery take Deadly Aspects.

Careful Aim (5 points) turns Intellect into attack power and is the way to Lone Wolf. Lethal Attacks (5 points) is 5% crit on everything. Surefooted is 3% hit, Strider Kick is a third melee special, and Clever Traps and Survivalist’s Discipline turn Immolation Trap into a damage button. Improved Tracking (5 points) is 5% damage against the creature type you track. Track covers Beasts, Demons, Dragonkin, Elementals, Giants, Humanoids and Undead, which takes in most raid bosses, so set it to the boss’s type before the pull whenever Track covers it.

The build skips the Marksmanship shot talents: Mortal Shots is ranged only, Hawk Eye is range on a bow you never fire, and Efficiency’s 15% comes on top of Resourcefulness’s 60%, so it saves little. The same build is the raid build. Rapid Killing (2 points) sits on Lone Wolf’s row, which Lethal Attacks and Careful Aim open, and takes two minutes off Rapid Fire, so a fight that runs past three minutes gets a second one. Its points come from Deterrence and Counterattack: behind a boss that is hitting the tank you never parry, so Counterattack never lights up, and Deterrence only answers a hit you are not taking.

rotation.prose:
Pet. In a raid, dismiss your pet before the pull; Lone Wolf only works with no pet out.

Aspect. From 30 to 59 Beast is your only melee aspect: put it up and leave it up. At 60 Aspect of the Falcon gives the same melee attack power as Aspect of the Beast (10 more with Hawk’s Ahn’Qiraj rank), and Deadly Aspects procs under either one, so Falcon is not a clear upgrade.

Mana. With Resourcefulness your mana holds through Raptor Strike on every swing and Immolation Trap on cooldown. Rapid Fire speeds your swings, so it is a melee cooldown for you.

Windfury. Wing Clip is only a filler while a Windfury Totem reaches you; in a group without a shaman, leave it alone.

Threat. Walk in behind the boss with the rogues once the tank has it; you sit on a fresh tank’s heels in the opener. Disengage trims some threat on a 5 second cooldown, but it turns off your auto attack, so start swinging again the moment it lands. Feign Death drops all of your threat if it lands; check the message, because either can miss or be resisted. Feign Death is also your answer when something turns on you.

Trash. Survival has little cleave of its own. Explosive Trap under the pack is your AoE, and Engineering’s explosives are the rest. Lay Freezing Trap before the pull.

Your white swings have a much higher cap that you will not reach, and hit past the special cap still raises white damage. Crit pays off on your melee specials: Predator’s Edge makes their crits hit for 230% of a normal hit instead of double, and every special crit keeps half your mana regeneration running through Resourcefulness. Night Elf for the Alliance: Elune’s Light’s crit feeds Predator’s Edge, so press it with Rapid Fire on the pull. Human’s Ruthless is next, and Dwarf’s 1% hit comes last even for a dual-wielder.

Orc and Troll are level for the Horde. Blood Fury goes on the pull with Rapid Fire and again at two and four minutes; Berserking stacks with Rapid Fire on your swings.

hunter/survival.professions: Your raid set asks for Enchanting. Molten Heart of the Mountain and Frozen Heart of the Mountain are Enchanting trinkets that bind on pickup, so nobody can make them for you. Heartseeker, the blacksmith’s dagger in your off hand, binds when equipped, so buy one and do not train Blacksmithing for it. Engineering gives Survival the AoE it lacks: grenades and explosives on trash. Skinning pays for your leveling.

leveling.early:
Levels 1 to 19

Train Heart of the Lion at level 1 and keep it up all the way to 60: 10% more stats and extra attack power (280 at 60) for everyone near you, and another 10% stats for you. Raptor Strike from level 1 is your main button, with new ranks at 8 and 16. Train Aspect of the Monkey and Serpent Sting at 4, Hunter’s Mark at 6, Wing Clip at 12 and Mongoose Bite at 16, which lights up after you dodge.

At 10 your trainer starts the taming quests, which end by teaching Tame Beast. Tame a beast at your level, feed it to keep it happy, and train Mend Pet at 12.

Your first five points go into Improved Tracking, 1% damage per point against whatever you are tracking: Track Beasts from level 1, Track Humanoids at 10, Track Undead at 18. Savage Strikes at 15 and 16 adds 2% crit to your melee abilities per point, then Survivalist from 17 adds 2% health per point.

Take quest rewards over vendor gear, Agility first. Replace the starting weapon with the first slow two-handed quest reward you find, since Raptor Strike adds its damage on top of the weapon hit. Wear leather until 40. From 40 you can wear mail, but keep a leather piece whenever it is the better one.
leveling.late:
Keep a pet out while you level: Lone Wolf is the last point this build takes, at 60, and until then the pet holds aggro and adds damage. Even at 60, out in the world a pet adds a little more damage than Lone Wolf and takes the hits, so keep it out while you quest and farm. Lone Wolf pays off in a raid, where you get the raid buffs and your pet gets none: dismiss the pet before a raid pull and call it back afterwards.

Open with Hunter’s Mark, send the pet, then walk in and queue Raptor Strike. Press Mongoose Bite whenever it lights up, and from 30 keep Lacerate on anything that will live long enough to bleed. Throw Immolation Trap under anything that will live long enough to burn, and Wing Clip a runner. Feign Death at 30 resets a bad pull.

Wear Aspect of the Monkey until 30: its dodges open Mongoose Bite. At 30 switch to Aspect of the Beast and keep it up. Aspect of the Cheetah at 20 is your run speed between quests, but it dazes you when you are hit, so never wear it into a fight. From 20 you can carry two weapons.

Talents after Survivalist:

  • 25 to 29: Predator’s Edge.
  • 30 to 39: Strider Kick at 30, then Resourcefulness, Expose Prey, Survivalist’s Discipline and Lightning Reflexes.
  • 40 to 42: Lacerating Strikes at 40, Lightning Reflexes full at 42.
  • 43 to 57: Deadly Aspects, then Lethal Attacks and Careful Aim.
  • 58 to 60: Rapid Killing at 58 and 59, Lone Wolf the last point at 60.

With a trap on every pull your mana runs short, so at a few levels you keep an older Raptor Strike rank on your bar: most of the hit is your weapon, so it does nearly what the new rank does for less mana, and the mana goes into traps. Drag the lower rank onto your bar from the spellbook.

  • 26 to 29: rank 3 instead of rank 4, once Immolation Trap rank 2 arrives at 26. On a Horde character rank 2 is better again: an Orc, a Troll or a Windshaper Skyborne at 26 and 27, a Tauren at 26 to 28. Put rank 4 back at 30.
  • 31: rank 1, while you have only the first point of Resourcefulness; it costs almost nothing. Put rank 5 on at 32, when you train it and the second point makes every rank cheap.
  • 40 to 45: rank 6, trained at 40, though a Troll does a touch better keeping rank 5 at 40 itself.
  • 46 and 47: rank 5 instead of rank 6, since the new Immolation Trap rank at 46 costs more.
  • 48: rank 7. On a Horde character rank 5 is still the better button: an Orc, Troll or Tauren at 48 and 49, a Windshaper Skyborne at 48.

talents.prose:
Combustion asks for 30 points above it. The Fire damage talents above it come to 26, and five ranks of Accelerant make it 31. Fire skips Blast Wave and Improved Flamestrike, which are AoE only, and Flame Throwing: 6 more yards are worth less to a raid caster than a faster Fireball. Two ranks of Burning Soul stay for the threat: 20% less threat from your Fire spells and a 47% chance to keep a cast from being pushed back.

The other 17 points buy hit and a little Arcane. Three go into Precision in Frost for 6% hit. Fourteen in Arcane take Improved Channeling, which opens the tree and keeps your Missiles from being pushed back, Arcane Concentration (a free spell 10% of the time), Missile Barrage, Arcane Blast and a point of Arcane Subtlety. Wand Specialization and Arcane Resilience do nothing on a boss, and Arcane Meditation’s regeneration is worth less than Missile Barrage and Arcane Blast, so all three are left out.

The level 60 build is the raid build with one change for the open world: Wand Specialization takes two of Improved Channeling’s points, because a leveling mage finishes mobs with the wand while the mana comes back, and 25% more wand damage is worth more there than pushback protection on Arcane Missiles. It spends its points in a different order on the way up. Swap those two points back into Improved Channeling when you start raiding.

rotation.prose:
Pre-pull. Mage Armor, Arcane Brilliance and your food buff go up. Conjure a Mana Ruby and a Mana Citrine and drink back to full. Start Pyroblast 6 seconds before the pull so it lands just after the tank’s first hit; its burn starts your Fire Power count.

Opener. Scorch to 5 stacks, and from there Fire Blast whenever it is ready, unless 3 Heating Up stacks have a Pyroblast waiting. Put up Arcane Blast once the stacks are on.

Combustion. Every Fireball, Scorch or Fire Blast crit inside it is an Ignite and a Heating Up stack, so the window usually ends in a 1.5 second Pyroblast.

Ignite and threat. Ignite’s damage is your threat too. Fire mages pull more than anyone else in the first twenty seconds, mostly off a Combustion window that crits three times in a row. You have no Ice Block and no Invisibility, so the only fix is not to pull: watch your threat, hold Combustion on a fresh tank, and stop casting for a global if you are close.

Mana in a 3 minute fight. Fire runs dry on a long fight, though not as fast as Arcane. In order: a Mana Ruby when you are 1,200 mana down, a Major Mana Potion the next time you are well down, then the Mana Citrine or a Demonic Rune two minutes after the Ruby. Gems and runes share one 2 minute cooldown, and the Robe of the Archmage has its own 5 minute one: use it whenever you are 625 mana down. After all of them comes Evocation, once a fight, with more than 30 seconds left.

Short on mana. Fireball stays your filler: Master of Elements hands back 30% of its cost on every crit, and the Arcane Missiles its Missile Barrage procs buy are free.

AoE. Flamestrike is a 3 second cast that burns the ground for 8 seconds, so cast it where the tank is going to stand, then follow with Arcane Explosion in the pack or a Blizzard from range. Two Flamestrikes at 990 mana each eat a third of your bar on a big pull before the Arcane Explosions start. Let the tank get a few seconds of threat first, and Frost Nova and Blink out if the pack turns on you.

Movement. Fire has no execute. On the move, keep Fire Blast on cooldown and save a Pyroblast on 3 Heating Up stacks for the next stop. Scorch’s stacks last 30 seconds, so a short movement phase does not drop them.

Frostfire Bolt is not a Fire filler. It hits for much less than Fireball, and its burn mixes Frost and Fire, which Fire Power does not count.

races.prose:
On the Alliance, take a Human: Ruthless’s crit turns into Ignite and Heating Up. Gnome is just behind: press Eureka! with Combustion on the pull and again the moment it is back.

On the Horde, take Undead for Touch of the Grave and a fear break. Orc is next: press Blood Fury with Combustion on the pull and on cooldown after that. Troll Berserking lines up with every Combustion, but falls behind both.

Skyborne can be mages only on the Alliance, and played without Read Leyline it does the least Fire damage of the lot.

mage/fire.professions: Take Tailoring and Enchanting, since your raid set needs both: Robe of the Archmage is a Tailoring craft and Frozen Heart of the Mountain an Enchanting one, and both bind on pickup, so nobody can make them for you. Enchanting also puts the spell power enchants on your own gear. The goggles in the head slot need 270 Engineering to wear: without it, take the best head you can wear and keep your two professions. Alchemy pays for itself once you raid every week.

leveling.early:
Levels 1 to 19

Fireball is trained at 1 with new ranks at 6, 12 and 18, so visit the trainer every even level. Frostbolt at 4 is your slow, Fire Blast at 6 is the instant finisher, Frost Nova at 10 buys distance and Flamestrike at 16 hits packs.

From 10 to 14 put five points into Incineration, 10% more crit on Fire Blast, then Accelerant at 15 to cut 0.1 sec off Fireball, and Ignite from 16 to 19 so every Fire crit burns for more.

Wand mobs down from half health to save mana: Lesser Magic Wand at 5 and Greater Magic Wand at 13 come from Enchanting, and Riptear’s Spare Arm (Rear Guard Patrol, Horde) or Elven Wand (Alliance, Bashal’Aran, Darkshore) are early quest wands. Your trainer’s level 10 class quest pays a staff or an orb; take the staff and retire the starter one. Wear cloth quest rewards over vendor gear, Intellect and Stamina first.
leveling.late:
Pyroblast comes at 20 and Ignite’s last point at 21, then three more points of Accelerant at 22 to 24 make Fireball a 3.1 second cast. Fireball stays your nuke through the 20s, with Fire Blast on cooldown. Then Scorch comes in:

  • 27: Improved Scorch’s first point lands a stack only one Scorch in three, so build the stacks only on a mob or elite that lives a minute or more.
  • 28: with two points, Scorch to 5 stacks first on anything that lives 20 seconds.
  • 30: From 30, with Heating Up in, Scorch and Fire Blast take over on single targets, and every few crits turn into a fast Pyroblast.

On leveling mana the cheap ranks win from here, because each one earns the same Heating Up stack for less:

  • Scorch rank 1 from 28 to 39.
  • Fire Blast rank 2 to 35 and rank 3 from 36 to 39.
  • Pyroblast rank 2 to 37, except rank 3 at 34 and 35.

Open on a mob with Pyroblast from range, Fireball (Scorch from 30) as it closes, and finish it with Fire Blast. Keep Frost Nova and Blink for anything that reaches you, and Frostbolt for kiting: none of your Fire spells slow until Frostfire Bolt at 40, and Frostbolt is still the cheaper slow after that. Flamestrike into Arcane Explosion clears packs once you have the Stamina for it. Train Mage Armor at 34 and wear it for the mana; switch to Ice Armor when you are taking melee hits in the open world.

After Combustion at 40:

  • 41 to 43: Precision for 6% spell hit: against a mob above your level every miss loses a whole cast.
  • 44 and 45: Wand Specialization, a quarter more damage on the wand you finish mobs with.
  • 46 to 48: Improved Channeling, which opens Arcane Concentration at 49 to 53.
  • 54: Arcane Blast changes the loop: Fireball is the filler again, as in a raid, with the Arcane Blast buff kept up.
  • 55 and 56: Missile Barrage turns its procs into fast Arcane Missiles.
  • 57: Accelerant’s last point makes that Fireball a 3 second cast.
  • 58 to 60: two points of Burning Soul, then a point of Arcane Subtlety, finish the build.

rotation.prose:
Before the pull. Drop Lightwell where the melee and the tank can reach it and tell the raid it is there: it lasts 3 minutes or 5 clicks, and being hit cancels a click. Fear Ward the tank if the boss fears. Prayer of Mending and Renew go on the tank as he engages.

On the tank. Renew stays at rank 7 or higher; go up to the top rank on a tank who is dropping through it. Leave Power Word: Shield on the tank to a Discipline priest: without the shield talents it costs more mana than it saves, and Weakened Soul locks it out for 15 seconds.

Stepping down. When the top Greater Heal would overheal or your mana runs short, step down to rank 1: a small heal wastes less on a small hole, so leave ranks 2 and 3 off your bars. Heal rank 4 is cheaper still, but it keeps only about half your bonus, so it is the last step down. With Divine Fury every one of them is a 2.5 second cast.

Low ranks. In Forever a rank learned far below your level gets less of your healing bonus: at 60, Lesser Heal and the first ranks of Heal and Renew heal for little more than their base, and Renew rank 5 and 6 and Heal rank 4 keep only part of it. Downrank only within the ranks you learned from your forties on: Greater Heal rank 1 is the one to keep.

Flash Heal at the top rank in a raid, a lower rank while leveling. Holy Binding heals you off every one of them.

Prayer of Healing is not limited to your own party: target a member of whichever group took the hit.

Pre-cast. Start Greater Heal on the tank before the boss swings and cancel it if he does not need it.

Inner Focus on a Prayer of Healing or on a Greater Heal for a tank who is about to drop. Do not let it fall on a Renew.

Assignments. On a group, Prayer of Healing is your main spell and Prayer of Mending goes on whoever in that group gets hit. Stay out of the boss’s cleave and the raid’s AoE: Twilight Focus helps, it does not make you immune.

Mana. Every heal you skip early is mana for the last minute. Major Mana Potion and Demonic Rune once you are down enough that neither wastes, Dark Sacrifice as an Undead, and a Gnome’s Eureka! on a string of Prayers of Healing.

races.prose:
Human for the Alliance. Spiritual Guidance turns The Human Spirit’s extra Spirit into healing, and Divine Grace is a free instant heal every 10 minutes.

Undead is the Horde pick, and the best Holy priest of all, for Dark Sacrifice: once a fight, trade your own health for well over a thousand mana while the raid is quiet, then heal yourself back.

Gnome is close behind Human. Eureka! works on your direct heals, never Renew, and Contingency Plan goes on the tank before a hard hit. Night Elf, Troll and Dwarf heal clearly less.

priest/holy.professions: Tailoring makes healing cloth you will wear into the first raids. Enchanting saves you the enchanting bill. Alchemy makes the flask and the elixirs you burn every raid, and that is the profession that saves a healer the most gold.

leveling.early:
Levels 1 to 19

Until Holy Fire at 20, Smite is your damage: Shadow Word: Pain at 4 first, Smite, then the wand. Power Word: Shield at 6 and Renew at 8 matter most, and Inner Fire follows at 12. Healing a group before you learn Heal at 16, keep Renew on the tank and use Lesser Heal rank 3 as your filler.

Improved Renew takes 10 to 12, since Renew is your main heal at these levels, and Holy Specialization 13 to 17. Divine Fury at 18 and 19 takes a fifth of a second off Heal.

Wear cloth, take quest rewards over vendor gear, and swap the starting mace for the first quest staff or caster mace. Get a wand early: a Lesser Magic Wand from an Enchanter at 5, a Greater Magic Wand at 13, or a quest wand such as the Elven Wand (Bashal’Aran, Darkshore) or the Cinder Wand (Arugal’s Folly, Silverpine Forest).
leveling.late:
From 20 you can keep leveling Holy in groups, or respec to Shadow at the trainer for faster solo questing and come back to Holy at 60. Solo, Holy is slow: Smite and Holy Fire hit hard, but they cost so much mana that you drink after every pull. If you level Holy, Holy Fire opens, Smite finishes, and Power Word: Shield keeps you casting.

Talent order:

  • 20 to 22: Inspiration.
  • 23 and 24: Twilight Focus, so most hits stop pushing back your casts.
  • 25: Holy Binding, the first level its row opens: your Flash Heals on the group then heal you as well.
  • 26 to 28: Improved Healing. Twilight Focus is full at 29.
  • 30 and 31: Litany of Light, then Spiritual Guidance, Spirit of Redemption and Spiritual Healing, so that all thirty Holy points are in for Prayer of Mending at 40.
  • From 41: Discipline. Twin Disciplines and Mental Strength open the row for Meditation, in by 53, then Inner Focus and Mental Agility.
  • 58 to 60: the last three points of Divine Fury close the build.

In dungeons, downrank early so a long pull ends with mana to spare:

  • Heal, 16 to 33: rank 1 is the filler through most of your twenties and early thirties: it keeps your whole healing bonus until 33 and heals more for its mana than any later rank. A later rank takes over at a few levels: rank 2 at 27 for a Human, Gnome or Night Elf (a Human stays on it at 28), rank 3 at 28 for a Dwarf, Gnome, Night Elf or Troll, rank 3 at 30 and 31 for an Undead or Troll, and rank 2 or 3 at 32 for everyone but a Troll.
  • Heal, 34 to 39: rank 1 has started to lose its bonus, and rank 4 costs more mana than its extra healing is worth in its first levels, so keep rank 3 from 34 to 37 before you move to rank 4, and to 38 as an Undead. A Troll stays on rank 1 at 34 and casts rank 2 at 38 and 39, and an Undead casts rank 2 at 39.
  • Renew, to 39: rank 1 through your twenties, except at 16, the level Heal arrives, when rank 2 is worth its mana. Rank 1 costs a fraction of the top rank and still keeps most of your healing bonus. Rank 2 and then rank 3 take over between 28 and 36, at levels that differ a little by race.
  • Renew, 40 to 60: rank 4 from 40, rank 5 from 45 and rank 6 from about 52 cost far less and keep all or nearly all of your healing bonus, so you can keep Renew up all dungeon. Rank 7 takes over at 59, already at 58 as a Human.
  • Greater Heal, 40 to 60: rank 1 as the filler all the way, even after rank 4 arrives at 58: a dungeon tank rarely needs the bigger ranks, so their mana is better spent on more casts. At 60, rank 3 and rank 4 heal about the same for their mana.
